arxiv-2506-03637.creator: Zhuohao Yu, Jiali Zeng, Weizheng Gu, Yidong Wang, Jindong Wang, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Yue Zhang, Shikun Zhang, Wei Ye
arxiv-2506-03637.description: Abstract Reward Models, essential for guiding Large Language Model optimization, are typically trained on fixed preference datasets, resulting in rigid alignment to single, implicit preference distributions. This prevents adaptation to diverse real-world needs—from conciseness in one task to detailed explanations in another.

arxiv-2506-16046.title: How to Increase Energy Efficiency with a Single Linux Command Rutgers Department of Computer Science Technical Report DCS-TR-760
arxiv-2506-16046.creator: Alborz Jelvani, Richard P Martin, Santosh Nagarakatte
arxiv-2506-16046.description: Abstract . Processors with dynamic power management provide a variety of settings to control energy efficiency. However, tuning these settings does not achieve optimal energy savings. We highlight how existing power capping mechanisms can address these limitations without requiring any changes to current power governors.

arxiv-2511-03358.title: Noise induced Stability of a Mean-Field model of Systemic Risk with uncertain robustness
arxiv-2511-03358.creator: Alexander Alecio
arxiv-2511-03358.description: Abstract . We consider a model for systemic risk comprising of a system of diffusion processes, interacting through their empirical mean. Each process is subject to a confining double-well potential with some uncertainty in the coefficients, corresponding to fluctuations in height of the potential barrier seperating the two wells.

pmc-10562672.title: TOAST: A novel method for identifying topologically associated domains based on graph auto-encoders and clustering☆
pmc-10562672.creator: Haiyan Gong, Dawei Zhang, Xiaotong Zhang
pmc-10562672.description: Topologically associated domains (TADs) play a pivotal role in disease detection. This study introduces a novel TADs recognition approach named TOAST, leveraging graph auto-encoders and clustering techniques. TOAST conceptualizes each genomic bin as a node of a graph and employs the Hi-C contact matrix as the graph's adjacency matrix. By employing graph auto-encoders, TOAST generates informative embeddings as features.

pmc-11626944.title: Low PPP2R2A expression promotes sensitivity to CHK1 inhibition in high-grade serous ovarian cancer
pmc-11626944.creator: Zhaojun Qiu, Deepika Sigh, Yujie Liu, Chandra B Prasad, Nichalos Bean, Chunhong Yan, Zaibo Li, Xiaoli Zhang, Goutham Narla, Analisa DiFeo, Qi-En Wang, Junran Zhang

Thus, innovative strategies are urgently needed to improve survival rates for this deadly disease. Checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) is pivotal in regulating cell survival during oncogene-induced replication stress (RS).

pmc-11655638.title: A biomathematical model of SARS-CoV-2 in Syrian hamsters
pmc-11655638.creator: Sibylle Schirm, Geraldine Nouailles, Holger Kirsten, Jakob Trimpert, Emanuel Wyler, Luiz Gustavo Teixeira Alves, Markus Landthaler, Peter Ahnert, Norbert Suttorp, Martin Witzenrath, Markus Scholz
pmc-11655638.description: When infected with SARS-CoV-2, Syrian hamsters (Mesocricetus auratus) develop moderate disease severity presenting key features of human COVID-19. We here develop a biomathematical model of the disease course by translating known biological mechanisms of virus-host interactions and immune responses into ordinary differential equations.

pmc-12949372.title: Structural Basis of MERS‐CoV Receptor Interactions and Antibody Neutralisations
pmc-12949372.creator: Edem Gavor, Yeu Khai Choong, Sunil Singh, Hariharan Sivaraman, Er Shi Yin, J Sivaraman
pmc-12949372.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Increasing outbreaks of coronaviruses underscore the importance of antivirals and vaccines that can combat a wide range of coronaviruses. Neutralising antibodies (nAbs), along with vaccines and small‐molecule drugs, are among the most promising treatments and prevention options against coronaviruses. Here, we focus on Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) and discuss receptor usage and current progress in antibody research against MERS‐CoV infections. First detected in Saudi Arabia and Jordan in 2012, MERS‐CoV is a lethal zoonotic pathogen.

pmc-13591813.title: Rapid choroidal neovascularization after non-flap internal limiting membrane peeling for macular hole in a patient with AMD: a case report and literature review
pmc-13591813.creator: Buğra Karasu, Büşra Yılmaz Tuğan, Enes Kesim, Serkan Özen
pmc-13591813.description: BackgroundChoroidal neovascularization (CNV) following macular hole (MH) surgery is a rare complication. While the exact pathogenesis remains unclear, previous reports in the literature suggest that it can occur in patients with pre-existing age-related macular degeneration (AMD) or macular drusen. In this report, we present a case that highlights the potential biomechanical triggers of this complication in an eye with AMD.

pmc-13613308.description: Patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC) face a poor prognosis, with limited treatment options and short progression-free survival. Oral vinorelbine, whether used alone or in combination with other agents, has demonstrated efficacy in treating metastatic breast cancer.
